items.name: Nile
facts: Sudan, Egypt, Uganda, South Sudan, Burundi, Rwanda +1 more
items.blurb: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeast Africa which empties into the Mediterranean Sea. At 7,088 kilometers long, it is the longest river in the world, although the volume of water it carries is much smaller than other major rivers such as the Amazon or the Congo.

items.name: Blue Nile
items.blurb: The Blue Nile is a river originating at Lake Tana in Ethiopia. It travels for approximately 1,450 km through Ethiopia and Sudan.

items.name: Amazon
items.blurb: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river in the world by discharge volume of water, and the second-longest or longest river system in the world, a title which is disputed with the Nile.

items.name: Yangtze
items.blurb: The Yangtze River, Yangzi River or Chang Jiang is the longest river in China and the third-longest river in the world.

items.name: Mississippi
items.blurb: The Mississippi River is the primary river of the largest drainage basin in the United States. It is the second-longest river in the U.S. after the Missouri.

items.name: Missouri
items.blurb: The Missouri River is a river in the Central and Mountain West regions of the United States.

items.name: Ohio
items.blurb: The Ohio River is a 981-mile-long river in the United States.

items.name: Colorado
items.blurb: The Colorado River is one of the principal rivers in the Southwestern United States and in northern Mexico. The 1,450-mile-long river, the fifth-longest in the United States, drains an expansive, arid watershed that encompasses parts of seven U.S. states and two Mexican states.

items.name: Rio Grande
items.blurb: The Rio Grande, in the United States, or the Río Bravo, in Mexico, also known as Tó Ba'áadi in Navajo, is one of the principal rivers in the Southwestern United States and in northern Mexico.

items.name: Columbia
items.blurb: The Columbia River is the largest river in the Pacific Northwest region of North America. The river forms in the Rocky Mountains of British Columbia, Canada.

items.name: Yukon
items.blurb: The Yukon River is a major watercourse of northwestern North America. From its source in British Columbia, it flows through Canada's territory of Yukon.

items.name: Mackenzie
items.blurb: The Mackenzie River is a river in the Canadian boreal forest and tundra. It forms, along with the Slave, Peace, and Finlay, the longest river system in Canada, the second largest drainage basin of any North American river after the Mississippi.

items.name: Hudson
items.blurb: The Hudson River is a 315-mile river that flows from north to south largely through eastern New York state.

items.name: Fraser
items.blurb: The Fraser River is the longest river within British Columbia, Canada, rising at Fraser Pass near Blackrock Mountain in the Rocky Mountains and flowing for 1,375 kilometres, into the Strait of Georgia just south of the City of Vancouver.

items.name: Madeira
items.blurb: The Madeira River is a major waterway in South America. It is estimated to be 1,450 km in length, while the Madeira-Mamoré is estimated near 3,250 km or 3,380 km in length depending on the measuring party and their methods.

items.name: Rio Negro
items.blurb: The Rio Negro, or Guainía as it is known in its upper part, is the largest left tributary of the Amazon River, the largest blackwater river in the world, and one of the world's ten largest rivers by average discharge.

items.name: Tocantins
items.blurb: The Tocantins River is a river in Brazil, the central fluvial artery of the country. In the Tupi language, its name means "toucan's beak".

items.name: Paraná
items.blurb: The Paraná River is a river in south-central South America, running through Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina for some 4,880 kilometres. Among South American rivers, it is second in length only to the Amazon River.

items.name: Uruguay
items.blurb: The Uruguay River is a major river in South America. It flows from north to south and forms parts of the boundaries of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay, separating some of the Argentine provinces of the Mesopotamia from the other two countries.

items.name: São Francisco
items.blurb: The São Francisco River, known in English as the San Francisco River, is a large river in Brazil. With a length of 2,914 kilometres, it is the longest river that runs entirely in Brazilian territory, and the fourth longest in South America and overall in Brazil.

items.name: Orinoco
items.blurb: The Orinoco is one of the longest rivers in South America at 2,140 km. Its drainage basin, sometimes known as the Orinoquia, covers approximately 1,000,000 km2, with 65% of it in Venezuela and 35% in Colombia.

items.name: Magdalena
items.blurb: The Magdalena River is the main river of Colombia, flowing northward about 1,528 kilometres through the western half of the country. It takes its name from the biblical figure Mary Magdalene.

items.name: Volga
items.blurb: The Volga is the longest river in Europe and the longest endorheic basin river in the world. Situated in Russia, it flows through Central Russia to Southern Russia and into the Caspian Sea.

items.name: Danube
facts: Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia +3 more
items.blurb: The Danube is a river in Europe, the second-longest after the Volga. It flows through Central and Southeastern Europe, from the Black Forest of Germany south through the Danube Delta in Romania into the Black Sea.

items.name: Rhine
facts: Switzerland, Austria, Liechtenstein, Germany, France, Netherlands
items.blurb: The Rhine is one of the major rivers of Europe. The river begins in the Swiss canton of Graubünden in the southeastern Swiss Alps.

items.name: Elbe
items.blurb: The Elbe is one of the major rivers of Central Europe. It rises in the Giant Mountains of the northern Czech Republic before traversing much of Bohemia, then Germany before flowing into the North Sea at Cuxhaven, 110 kilometres northwest of Hamburg.

items.name: Oder
items.blurb: The Oder is a river in Central Europe. It is Poland's second-longest river and third-longest within its borders after the Vistula and its largest tributary the Warta.

items.name: Vistula
items.blurb: The Vistula is the longest river in Poland and the longest river draining into the Baltic Sea, at 1,047 kilometres in length. Its drainage basin, extending into three other countries apart from Poland, covers 193,960 km2, of which 168,868 km2 is in Poland.

items.name: Dnieper
items.blurb: The Dnieper or Dnepr, also known as the Dnipro, is one of the major transboundary rivers of Europe, rising in the Valdai Hills near Smolensk, Russia, before flowing through Belarus and Ukraine to the Black Sea.

items.name: Dniester
items.blurb: The Dniester is a transboundary river in Eastern Europe. It runs first through Ukraine and then through Moldova, finally discharging into the Black Sea on Ukrainian territory again.

items.name: Don
items.blurb: The Don is the fifth-longest river in Europe. Flowing from Central Russia to the Sea of Azov in Southern Russia, it is one of Russia's largest rivers and played an important role for traders from the Byzantine Empire.

items.name: Ural
items.blurb: The Ural, also known as the Yaik, is a river flowing through Russia and Kazakhstan in the continental border between Europe and Asia. It originates in the southern Ural Mountains and discharges into the Caspian Sea.

items.name: Kama
items.blurb: The Kama, also known as the Chulman, is a 1,805-kilometre long river in Russia. It has a drainage basin of 507,000 square kilometres.

items.name: Northern Dvina
items.blurb: The Northern Dvina is a river in northern Russia flowing through Vologda Oblast and Arkhangelsk Oblast into the Dvina Bay of the White Sea. Along with the Pechora River to the east, it drains most of Northwest Russia into the Arctic Ocean.

items.name: Pechora
items.blurb: The Pechora is the sixth-longest river in Europe. Flowing from Northwest Russia and into the Arctic Ocean, it lies mostly in the Komi Republic but the northernmost part crosses the Nenets Autonomous Okrug.

items.name: Daugava
items.blurb: The Daugava, also known as the Western Dvina or the Väina River, is a large river rising in the Valdai Hills of Russia that flows through Belarus and Latvia into the Gulf of Riga of the Baltic Sea. The Daugava rises close to the source of the Volga.

items.name: Rhône
items.blurb: The Rhône is a major river in France and Switzerland, rising in the Alps and flowing west and south through Lake Geneva and Southeastern France before discharging into the Mediterranean Sea. At Arles, near its mouth, the river divides into the Great Rhône and the Little Rhône.

items.name: Seine
items.blurb: The Seine is a 777-kilometre-long river in northern France. Its drainage basin is in the Paris Basin covering most of northern France.

items.name: Loire
items.blurb: The Loire is the longest river in France and the 171st-longest in the world. With a length of 1,006 kilometres, it drains 117,054 km2, more than a fifth of France's land, while its average discharge is only half that of the Rhône.

items.name: Thames
items.blurb: The River Thames, or simply the Thames, known alternatively in parts as the River Isis, is a river that flows through southern England including London.

items.name: Po
items.blurb: The Po is the longest river in Italy. It flows eastward across northern Italy, starting from the Cottian Alps.

items.name: Ebro
items.blurb: The Ebro is a river of the north and northeast of the Iberian Peninsula, in Spain. It rises in Cantabria and flows 930 kilometres, almost entirely in an east-southeast direction.

items.name: Tagus
items.blurb: The Tagus is the longest river in the Iberian Peninsula. The river rises in the Montes Universales between Cuenca and Teruel, in mid-eastern Spain, flows 1,007 km, generally westward, and empties into the Atlantic Ocean at Lisbon.

items.name: Douro
items.blurb: The Douro is the largest river of the Iberian Peninsula by discharge.

items.name: Ganges
items.blurb: The Ganges is a trans-boundary river of Asia which flows through India and Bangladesh. The 2,525-kilometre-long river rises in the western Himalayas in the Indian state of Uttarakhand.

items.name: Brahmaputra
items.blurb: The Brahmaputra is a trans-boundary river which flows through Southwestern China, Northeastern India, and Bangladesh. It is known as the Brahmaputra in Assam, Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibetan, the Siang/Dihang River in the Mishmi language, and Jamuna River in Bangladesh.

items.name: Indus
items.blurb: The Indus is a transboundary river of Asia and a trans-Himalayan river of South and Central Asia.

items.name: Yamuna
items.blurb: The Yamuna is the second-largest tributary river of the Ganges by discharge and the longest tributary in India. Originating from the Yamunotri Glacier at a height of about 4,500 m on the southwestern slopes of Bandarpunch peaks of the Lower Himalaya in Uttarakhand.

items.name: Godavari
items.blurb: The Godavari is India's second longest river after the Ganges River, and drains the third largest basin in India, covering about 10% of the total geographical area. Its source is in Trimbakeshwar, Nashik, Maharashtra.

items.name: Krishna
items.blurb: The Krishnā River, in full Krishnaveni, in the Deccan Plateau is the third-longest in India, after the Ganga and Godavari. It is also the fourth-largest in terms of water inflows and river basin area in India, after the Ganga, Indus and Godavari.

items.name: Narmada
items.blurb: The Narmada River, also known as the Narbada or anglicised as Nerbudda, is the fifth longest river in India and overall the longest west-flowing river in the country. It is also the largest river in the state of Madhya Pradesh.

items.name: Mekong
facts: China, Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam
items.blurb: The Mekong or Mekong River is a transboundary river in East Asia and Southeast Asia. It is the world's twelfth-longest river and the third-longest in Asia with an estimated length of 4,909 km and a drainage area of 795,000 km2, discharging 475 km3 of water annually.

items.name: Irrawaddy
items.blurb: The Irrawaddy River is the principal river of Myanmar, running through the centre of the country. Myanmar's most important commercial waterway, it is about 1,350 mi long.

items.name: Salween
items.blurb: The Salween is a Southeast Asian river, about 3,289 km long, flowing from the Tibetan Plateau south into the Andaman Sea. The Salween flows primarily within southwest China and eastern Myanmar, with a short section forming the border of Myanmar and Thailand.

items.name: Chao Phraya
items.blurb: The Chao Phraya River is the major river in Thailand, with its low alluvial plain forming the centre of the country. It flows through Bangkok and then into the Gulf of Thailand.

items.name: Yellow River
items.blurb: The Yellow River, also known as Huang He, is the second-longest river in China and the sixth-longest in the world, with an estimated length of 5,464 km and a drainage basin of 795,000 km2. Beginning in the Bayan Har Mountains, the river flows generally eastwards before entering the 1,500 km long Ordos Loop, which runs northeast at Gansu through the Ordos Plateau and turns east in Inner Mongolia.

items.name: Xi
items.blurb: The Xi River or Si-Kiang is the western tributary of the Pearl River in southern China. It is formed by the confluence of the Gui and Xun Rivers in Wuzhou, Guangxi.

items.name: Amur
items.blurb: The Amur River or Heilong River is a perennial river in Northeast Asia, forming the natural border between the Russian Far East and Northeast China.

items.name: Lena
items.blurb: The Lena is a river in the Russian Far East and is the easternmost river of the three great rivers of Siberia which flow into the Arctic Ocean, the others being Ob and Yenisey.

items.name: Ob
items.blurb: The Ob is a major river in Russia. It is in western Siberia, and with its tributary the Irtysh forms the world's seventh-longest river system, at 5,410 kilometres.

items.name: Irtysh
items.blurb: The Irtysh is a river in Russia, China, and Kazakhstan. It is the chief tributary of the Ob and is also the longest tributary in the world.

items.name: Yenisei
items.blurb: The Yenisei or Yenisey is the fifth-longest river system in the world, and the largest to drain into the Arctic Ocean. Beginning in Mungaragiyn-gol in Mongolia, it follows a northerly course through the Krasnoyarsk Dam before draining into the Yenisei Gulf in the Kara Sea.

items.name: Kolyma
items.blurb: The Kolyma is a river in northeastern Siberia, whose basin covers parts of the Sakha Republic, Chukotka Autonomous Okrug, and Magadan Oblast of Russia.

items.name: Euphrates
items.blurb: The Euphrates is the longest and one of the most historically important rivers of West Asia. Together with the Tigris, it is one of the two defining rivers of Mesopotamia.

items.name: Tigris
items.blurb: The Tigris is the eastern of the two great rivers that define Mesopotamia, the other being the Euphrates.

items.name: Jordan
items.blurb: The Jordan River or River Jordan, also known as Nahr Al-Sharieat, is a 251-kilometre-long endorheic river in the Levant that flows roughly north to south through the Sea of Galilee and drains to the Dead Sea. The river passes by or through Jordan, Syria, Israel, and Palestine.

items.name: Amu Darya
items.blurb: The Amu Darya, historically known as the Oxus, is a major river in Central Asia which flows through Afghanistan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan.

items.name: Syr Darya
items.blurb: The Syr Darya, historically known as the Jaxartes, is a river in Central Asia.

items.name: Tarim
items.blurb: The Tarim River, known in Sanskrit as the Śītā, is an endorheic river in Xinjiang, China. It is the principal river of the Tarim Basin, a desert region of Central Asia between the Tian Shan and Kunlun Mountains.

items.name: Congo
facts: Angola, DR Congo, Republic of the Congo, Zambia
items.blurb: The Congo River, formerly also known as the Zaire River, is the second-longest river in Africa, shorter only than the Nile, as well as the third largest river in the world by discharge volume, following the Amazon and Ganges–Brahmaputra rivers.

items.name: Niger
items.blurb: The Niger River is the main river of West Africa, extending about 4,180 kilometres. Its drainage basin is 2,117,700 km2 in area.

items.name: Zambezi
items.blurb: The Zambezi is the fourth-longest river in Africa, the longest east-flowing river in Africa and the largest flowing into the Indian Ocean from Africa. Its drainage basin covers 1,390,000 km2, slightly less than half of the Nile's.

items.name: Orange
items.blurb: The Orange River is a river in Southern Africa. It is the longest river in South Africa.

items.name: Limpopo
items.blurb: The Limpopo River rises in South Africa and flows generally eastward through Mozambique to the Indian Ocean. The river is approximately 1,750 km long, with a drainage basin of 415,000 km2 in size.

items.name: Senegal
items.blurb: The Senegal River; Wolof: Dexug Senegaal, Arabic: نهر السنغال, romanized: Nahr as-Siniġāl, Hassaniyya pronunciation:, French: Fleuve Sénégal) is a 1086-kilometre-long river in West Africa; much of its length marks part of the border between Senegal and Mauritania.

items.name: Volta
items.blurb: The Volta River is the main river system in the West African country of Ghana. It flows south into Ghana from the Bobo-Dioulasso highlands of Burkina Faso.

items.name: Okavango
items.blurb: The Okavango River is a river in southwestern Africa. It is known by this name in Botswana, as Cubango in Angola, and Kavango in Namibia.

items.name: Murray
items.blurb: The Murray River is a river in Southeastern Australia. It is Australia's longest river, spanning 2,508 km.

items.name: Darling
items.blurb: The Darling River, is the third-longest river in Australia, measuring 1,472 kilometres from its source in northern New South Wales to its confluence with the Murray River at Wentworth.
